neighbours.label: an offer in a plea or bargain: what the speaker will give or do for the listener ('We'll do what you want', 'I will grant you three wishes')
fire: "Let my daughter go," the merchant pleaded, "and I'll pay you twice what she is worth."
The genie bowed low. "Release me from this lamp and I shall build you a palace."
"Don't shoot!" the thief cried. "Spare me and I'll tell you where the gold is hidden."
Kneeling before the king, the rebel said, "Pardon my men and we will serve you forever."
The dragon hissed, "Leave my eggs unharmed and I will give you safe passage."
"Please, put the knife down," he begged. "I'll do anything you want, just let her go."
The witch smiled. "Bring me the silver comb, and I will restore your sight."
"Stop the attack," the envoy pleaded, "and our city will open its granaries to you."
quiet: "My daughter left this morning," the merchant said, "and she paid twice what it was worth."
The genie bowed low. "I have lived in this lamp for a thousand years."
"Don't shoot!" the thief cried, as the guards dragged him from the vault.
Kneeling before the king, the rebel told the story of his long march north.
The dragon hissed and curled around her eggs in the dark cave.
"Please, put the knife down," he said. "Dinner is ready and the bread is warm."
The witch smiled as she combed her hair with a silver comb by the fire.
"The attack has stopped," the envoy reported, "and the city gates are closed."

notes: Card: top examples are pleas/bargains ('We'll do what you want', 'If you let me live, I will ease your pain'); probe: bargain offers ~0.24, a plain promise to clean a room ~0.02.
